description: A 'mepe' is one of two equal parts of a thing, a span, or a group: two people share a loaf and cut it so that neither piece is bigger. 'phanoi' (portion) is a part of any size. The word belongs to everyday speech and is no numeral, so an exact fraction in a record or a recipe keeps its own notation.
articulatory_notes: Voiced 'm' is hummed behind closed lips, which open on stressed mid front 'e'. A second closure, this time without voice, makes 'p', and the same vowel follows unstressed.
sound_symbolism: Two lip consonants and one vowel said twice: the word comes close to being two equal parts itself.
usage_notes: The whole stands before it: 'napa mepe' (half the bread), 'philo mepe' (half a day). People and countable things are plural there: 'lo miona mepe' (half of the people). Cutting a thing in half is 'muo wi mepe' with 'kati' (cut) or 'pisha' (split).

examples.phi: lo miona mepe to manolu. tasa mepe to wepu.
examples.translation: Half of the people stayed. The other half left.

examples.phi: no muo wi mepe ku ha lureko kati.
examples.translation: Cut this fruit into two halves.

semantic_domains.quantity: one of two equal parts of a whole
